proof_origin.place: Direct strict Roos proof using K-flat representatives

title: Closure of derived completeness under cones
statement: Let l be a prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X any scheme. Work in the unbounded derived category of internal modules over the continuous integral coefficient ring O_E pulled back from the profinite point to X_Proet. The canonical reduction functor at index n is derived extension to O_E/pi^(n+1). Completeness means invertibility of the specified zero-nullhomotopy Roos augmentation on a K-flat representative. For every distinguished triangle T, if its first two vertices are complete, then its third vertex is complete.

proof.text: Choose K-flat representatives P and B of the first two vertices. Write their derived morphism as a right fraction and take a K-flat resolution W of the numerator source. This produces a chain map W to B and a compatible pair of derived isomorphisms. Model-independence of completeness makes the augmentation on W invertible.

Shift closure gives invertibility of the augmentation on W[1]. The degreewise split mapping-cone sequence and natural Roos augmentation then give invertibility on cone(W to B). K-flat complexes are closed under cones. The standard cone triangle is isomorphic to the given distinguished triangle by its first two vertices, giving the desired complete representative of the third vertex.

theorem derived_nakayama_first_reduction_triangles
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∀ T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X)),
      T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X)) →
      IsDerivedComplete l E X T.obj₁ → IsDerivedComplete l E X T.obj₂ →
        IsDerivedComplete l E X T.obj₃
